messages:
maria: Quick doc dump — saw a p99 spike on INT8 KV path during the noon perf sweep. baseline FP8/FP16 looked fine. attaching quick numbers.
sam: Can you paste the numbers?
maria: sure — aggregate from 50k requests on same model, seq_len=128, prefix cache enabled. FP8 KV: p50=7ms p95=18ms p99=42ms mem_kv=1.0x. INT8 KV: p50=6.5ms p95=26ms p99=118ms mem_kv=0.38x. decode-quality delta ~= +0.8% perplexity (small) but some hallucination rate up on edge prompts.
raj: whoa p99 from 42 -> 118 is big. did kernel switch happen mid-batch? any kernel churn logs?
maria: yes, logs show kernel_select toggles whenever batch size >1 AND kv-hit-rate drops below ~0.7. we see frequent fallback to fp8 kernels during the generation window. snippet from router log: `kernel_select: int8_kv -> fp8_kv (latency_delta=0.22)`.
olivia: that switching likely causes CUDA graph teardown / rebind overhead + memory remapping. when a few requests in a batch prefer different kernels we serialize.
raj: can you share a sample trace?
maria: pasted trace (trimmed):
```
[trace] request A: hit_rate=0.92 chosen=int8_kv start=0ms
[trace] request B: hit_rate=0.45 chosen=fp8_kv start=0ms
[trace] scheduler: group( A,B ) -> kernel_switch to fp8_kv at 12ms -> stall 48ms
[trace] decode end A: 90ms
[trace] decode end B: 62ms
```
sam: so mixed-preference batching is the issue. kernel-switching penalty looks ~40-60ms when it happens during active batches.
raj: aside from hysteresis, can we do opportunistic left-pad batching: group by kernel preference before doing graph execution? but that hurts latency for solitary requests.
olivia: idea: add a micro-hysteresis in routing: only switch kernel if either (a) estimated speedup > 25% AND group_hit_rate > 0.6 OR (b) sustained for >3 consecutive batches. this avoids flip-flopping on transient hit-rate noise.
maria: also note calibration effects: the INT8 KV variant used a lightweight calibration (per-layer minmax) which reduced mem by 2.6x but increased decode variance on rare token distributions leading to larger KV miss-like behavior mid-decode. quant-noise might trigger different attention patterns which cascades into longer generation steps.
raj: interesting. quality regression small overall but the timing effect is non-linear due to batching. suggestions: (1) tune calibration thresholds to reduce outlier drift, (2) change batching heuristic to avoid mixing kernel prefs, (3) pre-warm kernel when swap is likely.
sam: can we reproduce deterministically? CI job?
ci-bot: perf-run triggered: `perf/kv-quant/2115001234-repro` started. status: queued.
raj: for repro, run with synthetic workload that toggles prefix hit_rate mid-request to mimic real traffic. and capture GPU event timeline.
maria: ran a repro locally: forcing hit-rate flips gave consistent ~55ms penalty per kernel switch. local numbers attached.
olivia: proposed quick patch: add `kernel_switch_hysteresis = 3_batches`, and a lightweight pre-check: if upcoming group has >30% mixed-pref requests, split into two subgroups (limit extra enqueue latency to 5ms).
sam: splitting with a 5ms enqueue cost seems acceptable vs 55ms crash. can we do adaptive split: measure real-time cost and adapt threshold?
raj: yes, add telemetry tag: `split_decision=[split|coalesce]` and record end-to-end latency delta. we can then autotune at runtime.
maria: open PR with heuristic and a small change to calibration runbook: require per-layer hist kurtosis check before enabling int8_kv. PR draft at: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/kv-quant/pulls/412
olivia: will review. also add a short-term mitigation: disable int8_kv for models with observed p99>80ms for 1 hour.
sam: agree. action items: maria -> repro artifacts & PR, raj -> telemetry flags & dashboard, olivia -> rollback guard.
maria: assigning and will dump repro logs into the perf bucket. thanks :thumbsup:
ci-bot: perf-run `perf/kv-quant/2115001234-repro` started staging-run on dedicated infra.
